Paris (mythology): Trojan prince, second husband of Helen of Troy.
Hailed as "the Lion of Verdun" for leading France to victory in that nine-month WWI battle, this marshal later headed the collaborationist Vichy regime — who is it?
Philippe Pétain: French general and dictator (1856–1951)
Proclaimed by Hitler from Prague Castle on 16 March 1939, this partially annexed Nazi territory covered the Czech lands after their occupation — which entity?
Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia: Territory of Nazi Germany (1939–1945)
Founded in 1997 by Lalu Prasad Yadav, this Bihar-based political party built its support among Other Backward Classes, Dalits, and Muslims — which party?
Rashtriya Janata Dal: Political party in India. The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD, lit. 'National People's Party') is an Indian political party, mainly based in the Indian state of Bihar.
This former Navy SEAL took part in the 2011 raid that killed Osama bin Laden and later stirred controversy by claiming he alone fired the fatal shot — who is he?
Robert J. O'Neill: US Navy SEAL (born 1976)
A Lemhi Shoshone teen who traveled thousands of miles from North Dakota to the Pacific with Lewis and Clark, she was later adopted as a suffrage-era symbol of women's worth — who was she?
This Germanic people had a semi-legendary hero named Widukind who fought against Charlemagne's Frankish forces — who were they?
Saxons: Medieval cultural group from what is now Northern Germany.
Centered on Marib and Sirwah in what's now Yemen, this ancient kingdom was considered the birthplace of South Arabian civilization and once expanded into the Horn of Africa. Which kingdom?
Sheba: Ancient South Arabian kingdom. Sheba, or Saba, was an ancient South Arabian kingdom that existed in Yemen before 275 CE.
An architect by training who once served as mayor of Quito, this man won Ecuador's presidency on his third try in 1992 after founding a new conservative party — who is it?
Sixto Durán Ballén: President of Ecuador from 1992 to 1996.
This Roman general became the first in the late Republic to march on Rome and win a civil war, later resigning his dictatorship after enacting constitutional reforms — who is he?
Sulla: Roman general and dictator (138–78 BC)
Rooted in shamanism and animism on the Eurasian steppes and centered on a sky god, this belief system was the state religion of the Mongol Empire — which one?
Tengrism: Religion of the Eurasian steppe nations.
Born in 1320, this ruler acceded to the throne in 1333 and became the last emperor of one dynasty and the first of its northern successor state after fleeing — who was he?
Toghon Temür: Emperor of Yuan dynasty from 1333 to 1368.
Head of state for nearly 26 years and often called an autocrat, this longest-serving Finnish president steered a policy of "active neutrality." Who was he?
Urho Kekkonen: President of Finland from 1956 to 1982.
Leading Russia's Liberal Democratic Party from 1992 until his death in 2022, this firebrand ran in nearly every presidential election and openly called for military action against NATO — who is he?
Once a loyal Nazi admiral running Germany's military intelligence service, he turned to sabotage and resistance against Hitler — and was hanged for treason at Flossenbürg in 1945. Who was he?

After his father — a former Andhra Pradesh chief minister — died in a 2009 helicopter crash, this politician toured the state on a consoling 'Odarpu Yatra' before founding his own party and later becoming chief minister himself — who is he?

Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, India. Jagan Mohan Reddy started his political career in the Indian National Congress and was elected as the Member of Parliament of Kadapa in 2009.
Pakistan's longest-serving de-facto ruler, this general seized power in a 1977 coup and held it until his death in a 1988 airplane crash — who is he?
Zia-ul-Haq: 6th President of Pakistan from 1978 to 1988.
Who among these was born first?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?

Oliver Heaviside (born 1850) is the earliest of the four. Although at odds with the scientific establishment for most of his life, Heaviside changed the face of telecommunications, mathematics, and science.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Aryabhata is an astronomer. The claim that Nalanda used to be located in Kusamapura/Pataliputra also cannot be proven.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Michael Atiyah is a mathematician. Sir Michael Francis Atiyah (22 April 1929 – 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.
What is the atomic number of Tin?
Tin is a chemical element; it has the symbol Sn (from Latin stannum) and atomic number 50.
What is the atomic number of Titanium?
Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.
In what year was Alexander Hamilton born?
Alexander Hamilton: Born out of wedlock in Charlestown on the Caribbean island of Nevis, Hamilton was orphaned as a child and taken in by a prosperous merchant.
In what year was Ivan Pavlov born?
Ivan Pavlov: Pavlov also conducted significant research on the physiology of digestion, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1904.
In what year was Archimedes born?
Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
In what year did Kalpana Chawla die?
Kalpana Chawla (July 1, 1962 – February 1, 2003) was an Indian-American astronaut and aerospace engineer who was the first woman of Indian origin to fly to space.
In what year did Rosalind Franklin die?
Rosalind Franklin: Rosalind Elsie Franklin (25 July 1920 – 16 April 1958) was an English chemist and X-ray crystallographer.
In what year was Oxycodone discovered?
Oxycodone: It is a highly addictive and commonly abused drug.
Mikoyan MiG-29: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The Mikoyan MiG-29 (Russian: Микоян МиГ-29; NATO reporting name: Fulcrum) is a twin-engine fighter aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
Which company manufactures BAE Systems Hawk?
BAE Systems Hawk: Hawker Siddeley. The BAE Systems Hawk is a British single-engine, subsonic, jet-powered advanced trainer aircraft.
Which country is Bombardier Challenger 600 series from?
Bombardier Challenger 600 series: Canada. At the end of 1975, Canadair began funding the development of LearStar 600, and then bought the design for a wide-cabin business jet in April 1976.
Who is credited with discovering Hassium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Hassium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
Who is credited with discovering HD 209458 b?
HD 209458 b: Michel Mayor. It is sometimes informally called Osiris.
Who is credited with discovering Osmium?
Osmium: Smithson Tennant. Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
This genus of succulent, spiky-leaved plants native to the arid Americas typically takes years to mature, with each rosette flowering only once before dying — what's the genus called?
Agave (Anglo-Hispanic) is a genus of monocots native to the arid regions of the Americas.
These mostly semiaquatic vertebrates are tetrapods that pointedly lack an amniotic membrane, splitting into just three living orders like the frogs and toads of Anura — what are they?
Amphibian are ectothermic, anamniotic, four-limbed vertebrate animals that constitute the class Amphibia.
Its Latin name means 'water-carrier,' and this zodiac constellation sits between Capricornus and Pisces, in a region of the sky nicknamed 'the Sea' for its watery neighbors — which constellation?

Aquarius (constellation) is an equatorial constellation of the zodiac, between Capricornus and Pisces. Its name is Latin for "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier", and its traditional astrological symbol is (♒︎), a representation of water.
Technically a giant member of the grass family, this plant's tallest species can grow stalks over 150 feet long and weigh up to 450 kilograms — what plant is it?
Bamboo are a diverse group of mostly evergreen perennial flowering plants making up the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.

A thin-leaved deciduous hardwood related to alders and hazels, this genus of trees is widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal climates, typically as a short-lived pioneer species — name the tree?
Birch is a thin-leaved deciduous hardwood tree of the genus Betula, in the family Betulaceae, which also includes alders, hazels, and hornbeams.
This American actor played Kyle Parks on Lifetime's The Client List before joining the cast of Revenge as Ben Hunter — who is he?
Brian Hallisay (born October 31, 1978) is an American actor, known for his roles as Will Davis in The CW drama series Privileged and Kyle Parks in the Lifetime drama series The Client List.
Nine to ten times as massive as the Sun and expanded to 71 times its radius, this blue-loop giant in the constellation Carina ranks second only to Sirius in night-sky brightness — which star?
Canopus is the brightest star in the southern constellation of Carina and the second-brightest star in the night sky.
Built under license from the Soviet MiG-21, this Chinese fighter jet carries the NATO reporting name Fishcan and specializes in short-range air combat — what aircraft is it?
Chengdu J-7 (pinyin: Jin-7; third generation export version J-7; NATO reporting name: Fishcan) is a Chinese fighter aircraft.
A scale insect native to tropical and subtropical parts of the Americas that lives on prickly-pear cacti, this parasite is the source of the natural dye carmine — which insect?
Cochineal (-eel, US also, -eel; Dactylopius coccus) is a scale insect in the suborder Sternorrhyncha, from which the natural dye carmine is derived.

Though Colin Maclaurin published special cases two years earlier, this determinant-based method for solving linear systems bears the name of the mathematician who generalized it in 1750 — what's it known as?
Cramer's rule is an explicit formula for the solution of a system of linear equations with as many equations as unknowns, valid whenever the system has a unique solution.
Caused by either too little insulin or cells that ignore it, this condition keeps blood sugar stubbornly high and comes chiefly in a type 1 and a type 2 — what is it?
Diabetes is a group of common endocrine diseases characterized by sustained high blood sugar levels.
Named from Greek roots meaning 'to repeat' and 'speech,' this automatic repetition of another person's vocalizations is closely related to echopraxia, the repeating of movements. What is it called?
Echolalia is the repetition of vocalizations made by another person; when repeated by the same person, it is called palilalia.
This former Google CEO co-authored the Unix tool Lex as a Bell Labs intern in 1975, later ran Novell, and in 2025 became chief executive of a rocket manufacturer — who is he?

Eric Schmidt (born April 27, 1955) is an American businessman and former computer engineer who was the chief executive officer of Google from 2001 to 2011 and the company's executive chairman from 2011 to 2015.

First recognised in the 1950s but not formally defined until 1990, this disorder of widespread chronic pain — often with fatigue and memory trouble — has no known cause and is treated multidisciplinarily. What is it?
Fibromyalgia (FM) is a long-term condition characterised by widespread chronic pain.
With about 37 species ranging from central Canada down to Costa Rica, this slender, keeled-scaled reptile typically sports longitudinal stripes in blue, yellow, or red — which reptile is it?
Garter snake is the common name for small to medium-sized snakes belonging to the genus Thamnophis in the family Colubridae.
This large, semi-bitter citrus fruit originated in Barbados as an accidental 18th-century hybrid of the sweet orange and the pomelo, and has also been called the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit (Citrus paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.

Known as 'The Last Universalist' for mastering nearly every branch of his field, this French mathematician and physicist founded modern chaos theory through his study of the three-body problem — who is he?
Henri Poincaré (29 April 1854 - 17 July 1912) was a French mathematician, theoretical physicist, engineer, and philosopher of science.
Often confused with a benign tumor, this cell-proliferation process increases an organ's cell count rather than the size of each cell — which term?

Hyperplasia (from Ancient Greek (hupr) 'over' and (plsis) 'formation'), or hypergenesis, is an enlargement of an organ or tissue caused by an increase in the amount of tissue that results from cell proliferation.
With the formula Fe2O3, this reddish inorganic compound occurs naturally as the mineral hematite, a key raw material for the steel industry — which compound?
Iron(III) oxide is the inorganic compound with the formula Fe2O3. It occurs in nature as the mineral hematite, which serves as the primary source of iron for the steel industry.

A civil engineer who commanded the Australian Corps in 1918, this WWI general was called by historian A. J. P. Taylor 'the only general of creative originality produced by the First World War' — who was he?
John Monash (27 June 1865 - 8 October 1931) was an Australian military commander of the First World War and a civil engineer.
This fatal prion disease, once common among the Fore people of Papua New Guinea, was nicknamed 'laughing sickness' and spread through ritual funerary cannibalism. What is it?
Kuru (disease) was a rare, incurable, and fatal neurodegenerative disorder that was formerly common among the Fore people of Papua New Guinea.
One of only five people to win multiple Nobel Prizes, this American chemist and peace activist is the sole person to have received two unshared Nobels — one in Chemistry, one for Peace. Who is he?
Linus Pauling (February 28, 1901 - August 19, 1994) was an American chemist and peace activist.

This colorless, highly water-soluble inorganic salt forms hydrates holding up to 12 water molecules per unit, and its anhydrous form is industry's main source for producing a lightweight, silvery-white structural metal — which compound is it?
Magnesium chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula MgCl2.
This nitrogen-heavy compound forms durable plastic resins used in dry-erase boards and dinnerware, and its foam version scrubs stains as the innards of a Magic Eraser — name the chemical?
Melamine is an organic compound with the formula C3H6N6.

An Egyptian who studied architecture at Cairo University and worked as a civil engineer, this man was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta (September 1, 1968 - September 11, 2001) was an Egyptian engineer, architect, and the lead terrorist hijacker for al-Qaeda on American Airlines Flight 11.
This stocky Arctic whale carries a spiralled tusk up to three metres long — actually a protruding left canine tooth thought to serve as weapon, tool, and sensor — what is it?
Narwhal (Monodon monoceros) is a species of toothed whale native to the Arctic.
This condition causes involuntary, repetitive eye movements, sometimes present from birth and sometimes acquired later in life, often reducing visual clarity. Name the condition?
Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
This genus of big cats contains the five largest living felines — jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard, and tiger — along with extinct relatives like the cave lion — what's the genus called?
Panthera is a genus within the family Felidae, and one of two extant genera in the subfamily Pantherinae.
Fill in the blank: “____ (born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur.”

Peter Madsen (born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur. Peter Langkjær Madsen (Danish: [ˈpʰe̝ˀtɐ ˈlɑŋˌkʰeˀɐ̯ ˈmæsn̩]; born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur.
This genus of single-celled parasites moves from mosquito to human bloodstream, destroying red blood cells and causing a disease with recurring fevers — what is this genus called?
Plasmodium is a genus of unicellular eukaryotes that are obligate parasites of vertebrates and insects.
Used to treat high blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms, performance anxiety and migraine prevention, this beta blocker medication reaches the bloodstream within 30 minutes of dosing — which drug?
Propranolol is a medication of the beta blocker class. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.
An Indian industrialist and philanthropist who twice led one of the country's biggest business groups, he descended from its founder and trained as an architect at Cornell. Who was he?
Ratan Tata (28 December 1937 - 9 October 2024) was an Indian industrialist and philanthropist.

Originally bred in Germany to herd livestock and pull carts of butchered meat to market until railways took over in the mid-1800s, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog now also works as a guard and police dog - name the breed?
Rottweiler (UK also) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.
First described in 1779, which large African raptor stands over four feet tall on stilt-like legs and is grouped in its own family, Sagittariidae?
Secretarybird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa.
Once placed alone in the genus Uncia before phylogenetics moved it into Panthera, this high-altitude cat ranges across the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayas — what is it?
Snow leopard (Panthera uncia) is a species of large cat in the genus Panthera of the family Felidae.

Starting with fever and flu-like symptoms before the skin blisters and peels into painful raw patches, this severe drug-triggered skin reaction sits on the same disease spectrum as toxic epidermal necrolysis, only less severe — which condition?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a type of severe skin reaction.
Defined as applying conceptual knowledge to reach practical goals in a repeatable way, this field covers both tangible machines and intangible things like software — what is it?
Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.
A nightshade-family relative of tobacco and the potato, this South American native arrived in Eurasia via the Columbian exchange and is botanically a berry eaten as a vegetable — what is it?
Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable.

Constantly produced by cells lining the lower female reproductive tract, this fluid mixture of liquid, cells, and bacteria varies throughout the menstrual cycle and helps lubricate and protect the area — what is it called?
Vaginal discharge is a mixture of liquid, cells, and bacteria that lubricate and protect the vagina.
This American child prodigy, son of a prominent psychiatrist, lectured on four-dimensional geometry at age 12 and graduated from Harvard cum laude at 16. Who was he?

William James Sidis (April 1, 1898 - July 17, 1944) was an American child prodigy whose exceptional abilities in mathematics and languages made him one of the most famous intellectual prodigies of the early 20th century.

Best known for the Cities of Salt quintet chronicling how oil discovery upended traditional Bedouin life, this novelist's criticism of Middle Eastern elites led Saudi Arabia to revoke his citizenship — who is he?

Originally launched in 2008 as Bombardier's CSeries, this five-abreast narrow-body airliner family was rebranded in 2018 after a European aerospace giant acquired a majority stake. What's it called today?
Airbus A220: Canadian narrow-body airliner family. The Airbus A220 is a family of five-abreast narrow-body airliners by Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (ACLP).
This military pilot became his country's first astronaut when he flew to the International Space Station aboard a 2024 mission — who is he?
Alper Gezeravcı: Turkish fighter pilot and astronaut (born 1979)
A towering 20th-century French mathematician known for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, he was a principal founder of the Bourbaki group. Who was he?

Latin for 'worm-shaped,' this finger-like, blind-ended tube branches off the cecum and, though long considered vestigial, may actually serve as a reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria. What structure is this?
Appendix (anatomy): Tube attached to the intestine.
Driven by elevated LDL cholesterol, this chronic inflammatory disease builds plaque lesions inside artery walls and can lead to stroke or coronary trouble — what is it?
Atherosclerosis: Inflammatory disease involving a buildup of lesions in the walls of arteries.
The only mammals capable of true sustained flight, this group flies on long digits webbed with a thin membrane and makes up about 20% of all classified mammals — what are they?

Named after two French physicists who discovered it in 1820, this equation in magnetostatics relates a magnetic field to the strength, direction, and distance of an electric current — which physics rule?
Biot–Savart law: Law of classical electromagnetism.

Completely dependent on humans for reproduction after millennia of selective breeding, this domesticated moth's caterpillars produce the raw fiber behind a 5,000-year-old Chinese industry — which species?
Bombyx mori: Moth mainly used in the production of silk.

Prescribed under the tongue, as a cheek film, an injection, a skin patch, or an implant, this opioid treats pain and opioid use disorder — often combined with naloxone in Suboxone to deter injection misuse. What is it?
Buprenorphine: Opioid used to treat pain and opioid use disorder.
Called 'rockmelon' in Australia and 'spanspek' in South Africa, this orange-fleshed true melon goes by yet another name in North America — what fruit is it?
Cantaloupe: Variety of melon. Originally, cantaloup referred to the true cantaloupe or European cantaloupe with non- to slightly netted and often ribbed rind.
Sold under the brand name Rocephin, this injectable third-generation antibiotic treats everything from meningitis to gonorrhea — which drug?
Ceftriaxone: Antibiotic medication. Ceftriaxone, sold under the brand name Rocephin, is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
The only member of the onion genus native to both the New World and Old World, this perennial herb has edible leaves and flowers and doubles as a natural insect repellent — what is it?
Chives: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
With a coat of dusky-grey blotches that inspired its common name, this wild cat is one of the few able to climb down tree trunks head-first, using a long tail for balance — what species is it?

Clouded leopard: Species of wild cat. Its head-and-body length ranges from 68.6 to 108 cm (27.0 to 42.5 in) with a 61 to 91 cm (24 to 36 in) long tail, which it uses for balancing when moving in trees.
Often defined as the transmission of information, this concept is famously modeled as a source encoding a message, sending it through a channel, and a receiver decoding it — what is it?
Communication: Transmission of information. Models of communication are simplified overviews of its main components and their interactions.
Unknown in the wild, this cultivated autumn-flowering plant has had its dried stigmas prized as the world's priciest spice for over 3,500 years — what is its scientific name?
Crocus sativus: Species of flowering plant. Crocus sativus, commonly known as saffron crocus or autumn crocus, is a species of flowering plant in the iris family Iridaceae.
Introduced in 1984, this turboprop regional airliner series was developed from an earlier company model and later gained 'Quiet' variants with active noise-cancellation — which aircraft family?

De Havilland Canada Dash 8: Canadian turboprop airliner. The De Havilland Canada DHC-8, commonly known as the Dash 8, is a series of turboprop-powered regional airliners, introduced by de Havilland Canada (DHC) in 1984.

The largest collection of fossils from this extinct Ice Age canine came from the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, though it roamed from South American savanna to North American forested mountains — what animal was it?
Dire wolf: Extinct species of canine mammal.
Its name comes from the Greek word for 'house,' and it studies organisms from the level of a single individual all the way up to the entire biosphere — which branch of biology is it?
Ecology: Study of organisms and their environment.
This branch of zoology, whose name derives from Greek words for 'insect' and 'study,' covers a field that has described over 1.3 million species — which discipline?
The only Old World member of its family to breed in the Northern Hemisphere's temperate zones, this migratory songbird winters in central and southern Africa — what is it?
Eurasian golden oriole: Species of bird.

An annual legume with leaves of three small leaflets, this semiarid crop has flavored dishes of the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — yet there's little clinical proof it works as the supplement people often take. What is it?
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.

This digestive disorder involves weak stomach muscle contractions that delay how quickly food empties into the intestine, often linked to nerve damage from uncontrolled diabetes — what's the condition called?
Gastroparesis: Medical condition. The opposite of this, where stomach contents exit quickly into the duodenum, is called dumping syndrome.
Built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine, this tripeptide is the most abundant low-mass thiol in most cells and a key antioxidant guarding against free radicals — what is it?
Glutathione: Ubiquitous antioxidant compound in living organisms.

Native to Africa and among the oldest of the chicken-like Galliformes birds, one domesticated species of this family wears a distinctive helmet-shaped casque and has been introduced worldwide — what are they?
Guinea fowl: Family of birds. Guinea fowl or guineafowl are birds of the family Numididae in the order Galliformes.
This localized pooling of blood outside the vessels — often triggered by injury, surgery, or blood-thinning medication — starts out liquid before clotting solid within the tissue. What is it called?
Hematoma: Localized bleeding outside of blood vessels. An ecchymosis is a hematoma of the skin larger than 10 mm.
Ashy-grey with a black head, throat and wings, this corvid was split into its own species in 2002 only to be folded back into its all-black relative by a 2025 reclassification — name the bird?
Hooded crow: Species of bird. The hooded crow (Corvus corone cornix), also colloquially called just hoodie, is a Eurasian bird subspecies of the carrion crow (Corvus corone) in the genus Corvus.

Defined as a blood sodium level below 135 millimoles per liter, this condition can arise from drinking excessive water — or even too much beer — and in severe cases causes seizures or coma — what is it?
Hyponatremia: Low sodium concentration in the blood.

Also known by names meaning 'water spinach' and 'kangkung,' this semi-aquatic tropical vegetable was likely first domesticated in Southeast Asia and thrives with barely any care near waterways — which plant is it?
Ipomoea aquatica: Species of plant. Ipomoea aquatica, commonly known as water spinach or kangkung, is a semi-aquatic, tropical plant grown as a vegetable for its tender shoots.
Serving as special adviser to the UN Secretary-General from 2002 to 2018, which Columbia University economist co-founded a nonprofit dedicated to ending extreme poverty?
Developed by a South Korean aerospace firm with Lockheed Martin and first flown in 2002, this supersonic jet trainer became the country's first indigenous supersonic aircraft — which aircraft family?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Family of South Korean jet aircraft. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.

Until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul split many of its 261 species into 25 new genera, this rod-shaped, gram-positive bacterial genus formed a major part of the human gut and vaginal microbiota — what genus?
Lactobacillus: Genus of bacteria. Lactobacillus forms biofilms in the vaginal and gut microbiota, allowing them to persist in harsh environmental conditions and maintain ample populations.
Traditionally kept as an indoor watchdog, this small non-sporting dog breed hails from Tibet — which breed?
Lhasa Apso: Tibetan breed of dog. The Lhasa Apso ( LAH-sə AP-soh) is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.
Sold under the brand name Cozaar, this angiotensin receptor blocker treats high blood pressure while also protecting the kidneys in diabetic patients — what drug is it?
Losartan: Blood pressure medication. Losartan, sold under the brand name Cozaar among others, is a medication used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
Known by the common English name 'mallow,' this plant genus bears palmately lobed leaves and five-petaled flowers ranging from pink to white — which genus?
Originally designated the DC-9 Series 80, this five-abreast single-aisle airliner first flew in October 1979 and entered service with launch customer Swissair the following year — what jet is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-80: Jet airliner model, series based on the DC-9.
In 2013, this tech billionaire took his own computer company private in a $24.4 billion buyout, the largest since the Great Recession, before it went public again in 2018 — who is he?
Making up about 23% of all named marine organisms, this phylum is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after the arthropods — what is it?
In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature into healthy ones, and some cases progress into acute myeloid leukemia — what is it called?
Myelodysplastic syndrome: Diverse collection of blood-related cancers.
Unlike its niacin cousin, this form of vitamin B3 treats pellagra without causing skin flushing, and as a cream is used to fade acne scars and reduce hyperpigmentation — what is it?
This soft-bodied mollusc can radically deform its shape to squeeze through tiny gaps and propels itself backward by jetting water through a siphon — what eight-limbed creature is it?
Octopus: Soft-bodied eight-limbed order of molluscs.
Also called a steer or bullock, and usually yoked in pairs, which castrated male bovine has long served as a draft animal for ploughing and hauling?
Ox: Common bovine draft and riding animal.
This economist and longtime New York Times columnist was the sole winner of the 2008 Nobel for his work on new trade theory and economic geography. Who is he?
Sold under the brand name Luminal, this WHO-recommended barbiturate treats epilepsy in children and can be given intravenously for status epilepticus — which drug?
Phenobarbital: Medication of the barbiturate type.
Caused by HPV and appearing on the sole of the foot with tiny black dots visible on its surface, this painful skin growth is treated with salicylic acid or freezing — what condition is it?
Plantar wart: Medical condition. A plantar wart, also known as a verruca, is a wart occurring on the bottom of the foot or toes.
Diagnosed only when symptoms like bloating, mood swings, and irritability disrupt daily life in the week or two before a period and resolve once it begins — what's this condition called?
Premenstrual syndrome: Emotional and physical symptoms that occur one to two weeks before a menstrual period.
This water-soluble organic compound, made of two fused rings, gives its name to a class that includes DNA's adenine and guanine bases — what is it?
Native to western Europe and known scientifically as Ribes rubrum, which widely cultivated berry has escaped into the wild across many regions?
Redcurrant: Flowering plant species in the family Grossulariaceae.

He dreamed up an "impossible" triangle, traded ideas with M. C. Escher, and shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for proving black holes are a robust prediction of general relativity — who is this English mathematician?
Roger Penrose: English mathematician, mathematical physicist (born 1931)
A pharmaceutical chemist with a Dartmouth Ph.D. by day, this American has chaired Anthrocon — one of the world's largest furry conventions — since 1999. Who is he?
Samuel Conway: American chemist and furry fandom personality.
